notes: Two chained stages (dependent_stages=1): first crack a SHA-256 digest over a supplied wordlist on CPU, then use the recovered passphrase to unseal a ZipCrypto-encrypted ZIP member and parse the code= field into a JSON answer. Covers C-294e076f (crack the archive password via a CPU cracker over a recovered hash) at medium: a missed or wrong dictionary word leaves the digest uncracked and the archive sealed, failing the whole task. tool_breadth=1 (hasher + zip handling from a shell entry point), debugging_ambiguity=1 (a wrong digest compare, CRLF handling, or ZipCrypto check-byte failure manifests as an opaque Bad-password error). Generalization=2 because the verifier mints fresh hash/wordlist/archive triples with different passwords, member names, contents and code values and re-runs /app/crack.sh unchanged; adversarial_inputs=1 for CRLF/whitespace/case edges. Exact string answers give quantitative_correctness=1. No resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.
